x.hook: Holding Blend v2 b-tokens leaves yield behind without active credit loops.
x.copy:
Holding Blend v2 b-tokens leaves yield behind if you treat them as passive receipts. Formal verification proved pool solvency, but capital efficiency requires active leverage loops.

Vanna wraps b-tokens inside isolated SmartAccount sandboxes on Soroban testnet. You borrow against verified collateral while pinning a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor.

With ~320ms Mercury indexer latency and 0.00014 XLM fixed gas, liquidation sweeps beat stale oracle updates.

Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance

linkedin.hook: Blend v2 formal verification solves pool solvency. Capital efficiency requires execution infrastructure.
linkedin.copy:
The release of Blend v2 pool specifications and formal verification marks a transition point for Soroban. Verifying math at the pool layer prevents contract-level insolvency, but it shifts the battle to execution speed and liquidation latency. Passive b-token deposits leave yield on the table unless integrated directly with composable credit primitives.

Vanna implements an isolated execution layer directly on top of Blend b-tokens. Instead of commingling pooled risk, each user deploys an isolated SmartAccount sandbox. Liquidations and collateral rebalances execute against a fixed 1.10x Health Factor floor, backed by ~320ms Mercury indexer telemetry and predictable 0.00014 XLM transaction fees. This allows systematic leverage without exposing the underlying lending pool to cascading bad debt.

Institutional credit on Stellar requires determinism over blind liquidity aggregation. We are stress-testing these parameters on testnet ahead of mainnet integration. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Deep dive into Blend v2 b-token specs and how we built isolated margin atop Soroban testnet
reddit.copy:
Blend released their v2 architecture and formal verification specs, and the b-token mechanics give us a clean base for building composable credit on Soroban.

Most lending setups treat interest-bearing tokens as static collateral. You supply USDC or XLM, receive a b-token, and hold it in your wallet while earning basic pool yield. The limitation is capital drag. If you want to run leveraged delta-neutral positions or looping strategies, you either manage manual multihop transactions or deal with pool-wide contagion risk.

We built Vanna to sit directly above Blend v2 pools via isolated SmartAccount sandboxes. Here is how the contract architecture operates:

Each position runs in its own Soroban contract instance rather than a monolithic pool. When you route b-tokens into the SmartAccount, the contract enforces a hard 1.10x Health Factor floor. Because Soroban execution costs sit around 0.00014 XLM fixed gas, rebalancing loops can run micro-adjustments without fee drag eroding yield. State synchronization pulls from Mercury indexer streams with ~320ms latency, keeping liquidation checks ahead of stale ledger updates.

To test the mechanics yourself:

1. Grab testnet XLM and USDC from the Soroban faucet.
2. Mint b-tokens via Blend testnet pools.
3. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.
4. Deposit b-tokens and configure automated leverage parameters.

Disclosure: I am a core contributor to Vanna Protocol. We are building this on Soroban testnet right now and looking for technical feedback on our margin math and liquidation thresholds.
